{{Short description|Iranian philosopher of the 6th century CE}}
'''Paul the Persian''' or '''Paulus Persa''' was a 6th-century [[Church of the East|East Syriac]] theologian and philosopher in the court of the [[Sassanid Empire|Sassanid]] king [[Khosrow I]] (r. 531–579). Paul's treatises on [[Aristotle]] would influence medieval [[Islamic philosophy]]. Notable works include his commentary in [[Syriac language|Syriac]] on Aristotle's ''[[Organon|Logic]]'', in which Paul declares the superiority of science over faith.<ref>Abd al-Raḥmān Badawī, ''Quelques figures et thèmes de la philosophie islamique'', Maisonneuve & Larose, 1979, {{ISBN|2-7068-0779-2}}</ref>

Paul may have studied [[Ancient Greek philosophy|Greek philosophy]] at the [[School of Nisibis]] in modern [[Turkey]] and at the [[Academy of Gondishapur]] in [[Iran]].<ref name="jackson" /><ref>Tjitze J. Boer, transl. Edward R. Jones, ''The History of Philosophy in Islam'', 1904 (republished 1933 as {{ISBN|1-60506-697-4}})</ref> Scholars have variously identified him with Paul of Nisibis<ref>C. H. M. Versteegh, ''Greek elements in Arabic linguistic thinking'', BRILL, 1977, {{ISBN|90-04-04855-3}}</ref> or Paul of [[Basra]].<ref name="jackson">[[A. V. Williams Jackson]], ''Zoroastrian Studies'', Kessinger Publishing, 2003, {{ISBN|0-7661-6655-4}}</ref> The administrative capital of the Sasanid Empire was [[Ctesiphon]] in modern [[Iraq]].

== Life and known works==
Paul the Persian is mentioned in the 9th-century ''[[The Chronicle of Seert]]'' and from the ''Chronicon Ecclesiasticum'' of the 13th-century [[Syriac Orthodox Church]] historian [[Bar-Hebraeus]]. These sources indicate that he was born in Dershahr in [[Persia]]. Bar-Hebraeus mentions that he lived during the time of the [[Nestorianism|Nestorian]] patriarch [[Ezekiel (Nestorian Patriarch)|Ezekiel]] (567-580). According to Bar-Hebraeus, Paul was a cleric in the [[Church of the East]] and well versed in [[Theology|theological]] and philosophical subjects.

Paul wrote two known works. One was an introduction to the philosophy of [[Aristotle]] which he delivered before [[Khosrow I]] and was later translated into Syriac by [[Severus Sebokht]].  This work was also translated into [[Arabic]] at a later date.<ref>D. Gutas, ''Paul the Persian on the classification of the parts of Aristotle's philosophy: a milestone between Alexandria and Baghdad'', ''Der Islam'' '''60''' (1983), 231-67, esp. 250-254 on the Arabic translation, attributing it to Abu Bishr Matta.</ref> The other work is ''On Interpretation'', which has never been published.

Both the ''Chronicle of Seert'' and Bar-Hebraeus record that Paul aspired to the office of [[Metropolitan bishop|metropolitan]] of [[Fars (East Syrian Ecclesiastical Province)|Fars]] and, failing to be elected, converted to [[Zoroastrianism]].<ref>[http://www.bu.edu/wcp/Papers/Medi/MediErha.htm Article on Priscianus of Lydia]</ref>  However, their claim is not otherwise documented and may be the product of the rivalry between the "[[Syriac Orthodox Church|Jacobite]]" Syriac Orthodox Church and the "Nestorian" Church of the East. The entry in the ''Chronicle of Seert'' reads:

{{Blockquote|[Khosrow] was very learned in philosophy, which he had studied, it is said, under Mar Bar Samma, bishop of Qardu, and under Paul the Persian Philosopher, who, being unable to obtain the metropolitan see of Persia, renounced the Christian religion.<ref>[[Addai Scher]], ed., ''Histoire Nestorienne (Chronique de Seért)'', [https://archive.org/details/patrologiaorient07pariuoft ''Patrologia Orientalis''], '''7''' (1910), 147.</ref>}}

== Works ==
* ''Prolegomena to Philosophy and Logic''<ref>''History of civilizations of Central Asia'', Motilal Banarsidass Publ., {{ISBN|81-208-1540-8}}</ref>
* ''Treatise on the Logic of Aristotle the Philosopher addressed to King Khhuosrowousrowau'' (in Syriac; British Museum ms. 988 [Add. 144660], ff. 55v-67rv; Wright 1872, 1872, p.&nbsp;1161);<ref>{{cite book|first=Byard|last=Bennett|chapter=Paul the Persian|chapter-url=http://www.iranica.com/newsite/|title=[[Encyclopaedia Iranica]]|access-date=2009-07-10|archive-date=2008-07-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080712124138/http://www.iranica.com/newsite/|url-status=dead}} Contains a detailed bibliography of works on Paulus Persa.</ref> translated into Latin by J. P. N. Land<ref>J. P. N. Land, ''Anecdota Syriaca'', vol. 4, v. 4, IV, Leiden, 1875</ref>
